title: Allow for the rest of this chat: ask row, settled marking, loaded-tab list
what:
panes/asks.js choices(): for an approval ask in perch mode with mode != yolo, add a row after `no`:
- bash: `allow "<command>" for this chat`. A command over 200 chars folds to its first line plus '(N chars, matched exactly)' and unfolds on click; it is never greyed for length.
- any other tool: `allow every <tool> for this chat`
- term_send: `allow every term_send for this chat (types into terminals without asking)`
- greyed with a reason for:
  - background calls
  - structural name rules ('eidolon asks about this call's shape, not its name')
  - asks whose call origin is unknown
core/state.js send(): a choice with allow:true posts hubPost('sessions/<id>/allow', {ask_id}) instead of the door's /api/answer. A 409 keeps 'answered elsewhere'.
The settled row with note === RULE_NOTE renders '→ yes · allowed by this chat's rule' (display only).
allow/list.js (a loaded section):
- 'allowed here': one row per rule, with its origin, and `[ revoke ]`
- empty: 'nothing: every ask comes to you'
- refetched on a RULE_NOTE settle and after a mode switch
tests:
allow.test.mjs:
- the row availability table (yolo none, background greyed, structural name rule greyed, unknown origin greyed, a 300-char command offered and folded)
- RULE_NOTE detection
- the payload is {ask_id} only; the page never sends a tool, command or origin
live_check:
fake perch on PORT=48136 with FAKE_ASKS:
- allow settles with the rule note, and a second identical ask auto-settles
- the loaded tab lists the rule; revoke
- a mode switch empties the list
risk: A script in the page's origin can turn any pending ask into a rule (attacker D is accepted, hub.md:300).
